Judgment

These three appeals are directed against the common order dated 04.12.2014( hereinafter referred to as "impugned order") canvassing a common question of law and facts and as such, it would be appropriate to dispose them of by a single judgment.

2. All the three appeals are directed against the impugned order passed by Sh. Vivek Kumar Tripathi, Ld. Adjudicating Officer/ADM (New Delhi), Govt. of NCT of Delhi whereby penalty of Rs.2,50,000/ each was imposed upon M/s FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.2 of 14 A.L.Chowdhary & Company,Supplier/ Distributer Firm(appellant in appeal no.2/15) & M/s The Claridges Hotel, Food Business Operator(appellant in appeal no. 3/15) whereas Rs.3,00,000/ was imposed upon manufacturing firm M/s Morde Foods Pvt.
Ltd.(appellant in appeal no.1/15) praying therein; to set aside the impugned order.

sentences.text: 3. The appeals were admitted for hearing.
Notices of all these appeals were given to the respective respondents who have resisted the same.
TCR was requisitioned.

4. The case of the prosecution, in brief is that on 12.10.2011 at about 4pm, Food Safety Officer Sh.Bal Mukand picked up four packets of 500grams each as sample of 'dark compound chocolate' from Sh.Neeraj Kumar Tyagi s/o Sh. Som Prakash Tyagi from the premises of M/s The Claridges Hotel (a unit of M/s Claridges Hotel Pvt.Ltd.), 12 Aurangzeb Road, New Delhi for analysis under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act(Packaging & Labeling) Regulations, 2011 ( hereinafter referred to as "FSSRs").

sentences.text: The said food article was found stored for human consumption at the time of taking sample from the said hotel.
The rest of the formalities were also conducted.

The Food Analyst analyzed the sample and found it to be misbranded vide report bearing No.PFA/Enf/585/2011 dated 18.10.2011 mentioning therein that the sample is misbranded because there is violation of regulation no.2.2.2.3 of the FSSRs as the label of the food article was found to be without declaration of nutritional information.

I have heard the rival contentions advanced on behalf of both the parties and have carefully perused the trial court record.

6. Feeling aggrieved, all the appellants have challenged the impugned order mainly on the grounds that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer did not conduct a fair inquiry and thus, he had erred to convict the appellants by imposing the penalty as detailed in paragraph 2 of the judgment.

Secondly; the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer had failed to appreciate the facts that the appellant M/s The Claridges Hotel was Food Business Operator (FBO) from whom four packets of 'dark compound chocolate' was picked up by the FSO in the same sealed condition as received/purchased from M/s Morde Foods Pvt. Ltd. ( Manufacturing Firm) through appellant/distributor M/s A. L. Chowdhary & Company who was neither the manufacturer nor the packer of the sampled commodity and thus, the defence of due diligence should have been extended to them and as such, they were liable to be protected by the warranty of M/s Morde Foods Pvt.Ltd. as provided in Section 80 (B)(2)(d)(i) of the FSS Act,
2006.

Thirdly, the Ld. Adjudicating Officer had failed to appreciate that an item of packaged food which is ready for personal consumption by persons or families would cease to be pre  packaged or pre  packed food if purchased by an industrial consumer.

To support his contentions, he has placed reliance upon the following judgment: Danisco(India) Private Limited Vs. Union of India and another,2014(2) FAC 109 wherein His Lordship was pleased to make the following observations:

sentences.text: 7. Per contra, the Ld. Special PP has refuted the entire line of arguments whilst making submissions that the FBO firm was found storing misbranded food which did not contain any nutritional information being a food item meant for human consumption.

They cannot claim any defence that only supplier and manufacturer are liable as they too carry out such mandatory checks of the food concerned being used for human consumption in any preparatory form.

It needs to be noticed that the sampled article was kept for human consumption which is opined to be misbranded by the Public Analyst because of violation of Regulation No.2.2.2.3. of the FSSRs and as such, it comes within the mischief of Section 26 (2)(ii) of the FSS Act read with Section 3(1)(zf)( C)(i) of FSS Act which is punishable u/s 52 of the FSS Act.
8.

First and foremost point raised by the Ld. Counsels for the appellants is that appellant M/s A.L.Chowdhary & Company, a partnership firm is engaged in distribution of cocoa products like dark compound chocolate manufactured by M/s Morde Foods Pvt. Ltd.

The food article is sold in bulk packages to be used as raw material / intermediate product / ingredient by industries/institutions like hotels, air lines & other companies who may use it to manufacture other bakery and FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.6 of 14 confectionery items etc. which was not for sale directly to the consumer in the same form.
The sampled food article could be used only under controlled temperatures by processing/melting by the skilled/expert employees of the industries for its proper usages to make their own end product.

As per the Public Analyst Report, the sampled food article was not found adulterated but the same was opined to be misbranded on account of non declaring the nutritional information on the label of the packages.
It is further argued that nutritional information is not required to be mentioned on the packages of the food articles which are not meant for direct consumption by consumers.
As the sampled commodity was to be used as raw material / intermediate product needed by industries to make their own end product and as such, the impugned order is not sustainable under the law.
9. Section 2 (ix) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 describes 'misbranding' of an article of food.

The relevant clause 'k' relating to label reads as under :
"2(ix) misbranded an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded - (a) to (j).....
(k) If it is not labeled in accordance with the requirements of this Act or Rules made thereunder".

sentences.text: The controversy whether the Labelling Regulations apply to the goods in question has to be considered in view of the context as discussed above.

It is alleged by FSSAI that the goods are non compliant with regulation 2.2.2:2 of the Labelling Regulations and it is, therefore,
necessary to refer to the relevant clauses of regulation 2.2.2 which is quoted below: "2.2.2:
Labelling of Prepackaged Foods

In addition to the General Labelling requirements specified in 2.2.1 above every package of food shall carry the following information on the label, namely,
1. The Name of Food: The name of the food shall include trade name or description of food contained in the package.
2. List of Ingredients:
As is, plainly, apparent from the heading of Regulation 2.2.2, the same is applicable in respect of "Pre packaged" foods.
The opening words of the Regulation 2.2.2 also indicate that the requirement to carry labels is with respect to a "package" of food.
The expression "Prepackaged" is defined under Regulation 1.2.1:8 of the Labelling Regulations.

The said Regulation reads as under:
"8. "Prepackaged" or "Prepacked food", means food, which is placed in a package of any nature,
in such a manner that the contents cannot be changed without tampering it and which is ready for sale to the consumer;
Note: The expression "package" wherever it FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.8 of 14 occurs in these Regulations, shall be construed as package containing pre packed food articles."
20.

sentences.text:
The expression 'consumer' has not been defined under the Labelling Regulations but is defined under Section 3(1)(f) of the FSS Act as under: "(f) "consumer" means persons and families purchasing and receiving food in order to meet their personal needs;"
21.

It is apparent from the conjoint reading of Regulation 1.2.1:8 with Clause (f) of Section 3(1) of the FSS Act that a prepackaged or prepacked food would mean food which is ready for sale to persons and families purchasing and receiving food in order to meet their personal needs.
22. In my view, the expression 'personal needs' would be determinative of the manner in which the expression 'persons and families' as used in Section 3(1)(f) of the FSS Act ought to be interpreted.

sentences.text: 5 The expression 'personal needs' plainly implies personal consumption.

The word 'personal',
according to Oxford English Dictionary, Fifth Edition, inter alia, means "pertaining to, concerning,
or affecting a person as an individual (rather than as a member of a group or of the public, or in a professional capacity etc.)".
In the given context of food consumption, the expression 'personal needs' of 'persons and families' would only imply needs of individuals.

The words 'persons and families' would in the present context mean individuals and families and applying the principle of ejusdem generis, the word 'persons' would exclude any corporate or any juridical entity and only mean natural persons.
Plainly, purchase or receipt of food for personal consumption is the operative condition before a person or family, qualify as 'consumer' within the definition of Section 3(1)(f) of the FSS Act.

Thus, an industrial user or an entity which purchases food items for utilising the same in their production process would be excluded from the definition of the expression 'consumer'
within the meaning of Section 3(1)(f) of the FSS Act.

It, therefore, follows that products which fall under the definition of food, meant not for direct human consumption but for sale to industrial FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.9 of 14 consumers for use in manufacture of articles of food, would be excluded from the definition of 'prepackaged' or 'pre packed food'.

entities.text: FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.9 of 14
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
This, of course,
does not mean that an item of packaged food, which is ready for personal consumption by persons or families, would cease to be prepackaged food or prepacked food if purchased by an industrial consumer.

As long as packaged food contains food items, which are ready for personal consumption,
the same would fall within the definition of prepackaged or prepacked food.
And, items that are not meant for direct consumption by individuals would fall completely outside the definition of pre packaged or prepacked food.
Applying the aforesaid tests, it is apparent that the goods in question are not items of prepackaged or prepacked food.

sentences.text: The allegation of misbranding against the appellants were that the sampled product was without declaration of nutritional information on the label of the packages.
Although no reason has been given by the Analyst for declaring the sample to be misbranded.
The objective of the declaration of the label was that the purchaser should know at the time of purchase as to whether the article being purchased was capable of being used and till what time.

But in the instant case, food article dark compound chocolate is sold in the bulk packages to be used as raw material/ intermediate product by the industries/ institutions like hotels, airlines which are not meant for direct sale to the consumers in the same form.

Infact, it was to be used by the industries/ institutions like hotel,
airlines for manufacturing bakery and other confectionery items only under controlled temperatures by processing/melting with the help of expert/specialized employees for its proper usage to make their own end product.
Thus, it can be well said that such type of food items would not fall within the definition of pre  packaged or pre  packed food.

13. Now, I am coming to the next plea of the appellants namely M/s A.L. Chowdhary & Company and The Claridges Hotel that they were liable to be protected by the warranty of the manufacturing appellant M/s Morde Foods Pvt.Ltd. as provided u/s. 80 (B)(2)(d)(i) of the FSS Act, 2006.

15. If the facts of the cases of both the appellants namely M/s A.L.Chowdhary & Company and The Claridges Hotel are examined in the light of the section as referred to above, it makes clear that the food article dark compound chocolate was purchased in bulk packages by the appellant firm M/s A.L. Chowdhary & Company from M/s Morde Foods Pvt. Ltd. being distributor of cocoa products and sold the same to M/s The Claridges Hotel in the same intact condition which was received from the manufacturing company.

The Claridges Hotel purchased the food article dark compound chocolate for its own use in preparation of desserts for sale to its customers and M/s The Claridges Hotel did not sell the dark compound chocolate product directly to the consumers in the same form.

The aforesaid sampled food FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.12 of 14 article was meant to be sold by the manufacturing company in the bulk packages only of 20 slabs of 500 grams each in sealed carton box with all required label/declaration except nutritional information because the food article was meant for institutional use and not for retail sale.

sentences.text: Both the appellants namely M/s A.L.Chowdhary & Company and M/s The Claridges Hotel were not manufacturer/packer of the sampled commodity and the sampled commodity was taken by the FSO in the same sealed condition as received/purchased from M/s Morde Foods Pvt. Ltd. and as such, they cannot be held responsible for nonprinting the declaration on the label of the sampled commodity.

Admittedly, the sampled commodity was not meant for direct sale to consumers in that form and was an intermediately product to be used in making other finished products,therefore, I find force in the contention of both the appellants namely M/s A.L.Chowdhary & Company and M/s The Claridges Hotel.

16. On the basis of reappreciation of the material including the evidence from the trial court record, I am of the considered view that the court of Ld. Adjudicating Officer fell into an error and failed to appreciate the attended circumstances with the adduced material including the documents such as Public Analyst Report in a proper legal perspective and in this regard, the order of the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer is vitiated with error of law, impropriety and misappreciation of the material and in this context, I feel every justification to interfere in the impugned order passed by the Ld.Adjudicating Officer.
Thus, the impugned order dated 04.12.2014 is FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.13 of 14 set aside by accepting the appeals.

But in the instant case, food article dark compound chocolate is sold in the bulk packages to be used as raw material/ intermediate product by the industries/ institutions like hotels, airlines which are not meant for direct sale to the consumers in the same form.
Thus, it can be well said that such type of food items would not fall within the definition of pre  packaged or pre  packed food.
The Claridges Hotel purchased the food article dark compound chocolate for its own use in preparation of desserts for sale to its customers and M/s The Claridges Hotel did not sell the dark compound chocolate product directly to the consumers in the same form.
Both the appellants namely M/s A.L.Chowdhary & Company and M/s The Claridges Hotel were not manufacturer/packer of the sampled commodity and the sampled commodity was taken by the FSO in the same sealed condition as received/purchased from M/s Morde Foods Pvt. Ltd. and as such, they cannot be held responsible for nonprinting the declaration on the label of the sampled commodity.
16. On the basis of reappreciation of the material including the evidence from the trial court record, I am of the considered view that the court of Ld. Adjudicating Officer fell into an error and failed to appreciate the attended circumstances with the adduced material including the documents such as Public Analyst Report in a proper legal perspective and in this regard, the order of the Ld.
Adjudicating Officer is vitiated with error of law, impropriety and misappreciation of the material and in this context, I feel every justification to interfere in the impugned order passed by the Ld.Adjudicating Officer.
opennyai_summary.decision:
13. Now, I am coming to the next plea of the appellants namely M/s A.L. Chowdhary & Company and The Claridges Hotel that they were liable to be protected by the warranty of the manufacturing appellant M/s Morde Foods Pvt.Ltd. as provided u/s. 80 (B)(2)(d)(i) of the FSS Act, 2006.
Thus, the impugned order dated 04.12.2014 is FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.13 of 14 set aside by accepting the appeals.
